done_when: The commit hook refuses only when git commit itself is given -n or --no-verify, never for an -n that belongs to another command on the same line

findings.body:
Raise: Security. `_without_data` checks for comments separately on each line. In `echo x\
#note; git commit -n`, the shell removes the backslash and newline before parsing, so `#note` becomes part of `x#note` and the commit runs. The scanner instead treats the second line as a comment and removes the prohibited commit. The escaped-space test does not cover this line-continuation form.
findings.title: Backslash continuation can hide a commit that skips hooks

findings.body: Raise: Not done. The heredoc check recognizes a stdin commit message only when the command starts with literal `git` and uses the listed spellings of `-F -` or `--file=-`. For `env GIT_EDITOR=: git commit --file=- <<'EOF'` with a message line mentioning `git commit -n`, the body is retained and parsed as a command, so Forge refuses a commit that has no prohibited option. The named proof covers `git -C web commit --file=-`, but not this normal command prefix.
